San Francisco & the whole Bay · times verified Aug 6

This Weekend in the Bay

Friday–Sunday, August 7–9, 2026

Outside Lands swallows Golden Gate Park all three days — so this guide is deliberately built around it. What's left is an unusually good weekend: a Situationist film retrospective with the translator in the room, the biennial aerial-arts festival, Joan Baez opening a circus under a big top in Alameda, three West Edge operas, the Bach Festival's finale, and a 176-speaker sound theater in total darkness. Filter by day and region; every card links to the event's own page.

🎪 SF Aerial Arts Fest — biennial 🎼 SF Bach Festival finale + West Edge Opera 🎬 Guy Debord retrospective at ATA 🎞️ Robert Townsend residency wraps 🎡 First Friday: Oakland · North Beach · San José ⚠️ Outside Lands — avoid Golden Gate Park
TOP PICK our pick of the category ★ CRITICS’ flagged by a named outlet ✦ RARE / UNUSUAL scarce or one-of-a-kind

Top 5 This Weekend

The five best things across every category — chosen for rarity and variety, not five of a kind.

01 · IMMERSIVE

The Soiled Dove — Opening Night

Fri Aug 7, doors 7:30pm (+ Sat Aug 8)
The Big Top at Radium Runway · Alameda

Vau de Vire's Barbary-Coast dinner-circus opens its 2026 season under a 12,000-sq-ft Italian big top — a brand-new storyline, ragtime by Sgt. Splendor, circus acts at your table, and Joan Baez billed with the cast. Opening night only comes once.

02 · CINEMA

The Films of Guy Debord

Fri Aug 7 & Sat Aug 8, 7pm · $10
Artists’ Television Access · Mission, SF

Debord's anti-cinema was pulled from circulation for two decades after his producer's unsolved assassination. Ken Knabb — his English translator — introduces each program in person and takes questions. Ten dollars for something that almost never screens.

03 · AERIAL

SF Aerial Arts Festival

Fri–Sun, 9 programs · $15–$75
Fort Mason Center · Marina, SF

Zaccho Dance Theatre's seventh biennial — it only happens every two years. Site-responsive aerial work made for a pier shed, world premieres from Amelia Rudolph and Megan Lowe, and a free three-day festival of aerial-dance films in the Grey Box Gallery.

04 · OPERA

West Edge Opera: Handel’s Rinaldo

Sat Aug 8, 8pm · $22–$182
Oakland Scottish Rite Center · Oakland

Handel's Baroque magic-opera restaged as a comic-book superhero romp, with countertenor Kyle Tingzon in the title role. SF Classical Voice called it "a superhero romp with heart." Only three performances exist.

05 · SOUND ART

Audium: “Hidden Currents”

Fri & Sat, 8pm · $20–$30
Audium · Lower Nob Hill, SF

176 speakers, 49 seats, total darkness — and a brand-new commissioned work by golden lionheart collier tracing the routes of forced migration across the African diaspora. There is nothing else like this room anywhere.

Gary Owen’s 75-minute monologue — Effie, in a nowhere Welsh town, carrying a cost the state won’t name. Alicia Mason alone on stage, in Shotgun’s first one-person production in 34 years. A Guardian top-50 play of the century.

Repertory Cinema

11 films

An exceptional repertory weekend, listed film by film. Robert Townsend’s artist residency at the 4-Star wraps Sunday; BAMPFA has four in-person guests and two restorations; and there is celluloid at the Balboa, the Castro and the Grand Lake.

🎞️
TOP PICK✦ Translator in person
Situationist cinemaFri & Sat 7pm

The Cinema Must Be Destroyed: The Films of Guy Debord

Artists’ Television Access · Mission, SF
$10

Friday brings four early shorts (1952–61); Saturday, the feature-length Society of the Spectacle, Debord’s détournement of his own book. Withdrawn from circulation for two decades after his producer’s unsolved assassination — and Ken Knabb, his English translator, introduces each program.

Pair: Buddy (fit 4.6) — chef-driven natural-wine bar on 22nd St, five minutes’ walk and open late.

Oddities & One-Offs

9 finds

The small, strange, only-this-weekend end of the calendar — experimental music in warehouses and living rooms, historic telescopes, and a swap meet that happens seven times a year.

Live cinemaSat 7pm (doors 6:30)

Benefit for Shapeshifters Cinema: It Could Be ∞ + Dyemark

Shapeshifters Cinema · West Oakland
$8–$88 sliding scale

CCA’s illustration chair draws live while three musicians improvise a score, audience members aim hand-held projectors around the room, and Nat Swope runs Super 8. The opener interprets three 16mm films with acoustic interventions. Forty seats.

Free improv + poetrySun 5pm

Jon Raskin + Carla Harryman

Spruce Street Concerts, private home · Berkeley
$30 · address given on RSVP

Four decades of duo work between a founding member of the ROVA Saxophone Quartet and one of the central figures of Language poetry — performed in somebody’s living room. The intersection of two favourite lanes, at the smallest possible scale.

🔭
✦ Free · clear skies only
AstronomyFri & Sat 7:30–10:30pm

Chabot Free Telescope Viewings

Chabot Space & Science Center · Oakland Hills
Free

Three historic domes open to anyone who turns up: Leah, an 8-inch Alvan Clark refractor from 1883; Rachel, a 20-inch from 1916 and the largest refractor in the West regularly open to the public; and the 36-inch Nellie. Check the humidity readout before driving up — the refractors close above 90%.

✦ Only 7 dates a year
Swap meetSat 6am–noon

Electronics Flea Market

West Valley College, Lot 2 · Saratoga
Free for buyers · free parking in Lot 2

The Bay’s legendary second-Saturday ham-radio and vintage-electronics swap — retro receivers, test gear, salvage, hobbyist oddments, spread across a college parking lot. It only runs March through September, so there are seven of these a year. Go early.

✦ Never repeats
Experimental theaterFri & Sat 9pm

The Infinite Wrench: 30 Plays in 60 Minutes

SF Neo-Futurists, 447 Minna St · SoMa, SF
$13 plus the roll of a die at the door

Thirty two-minute plays, performed in whatever order the audience shouts out, with the price of admission decided by a die. The menu changes every single week, so the show you see has never existed before and won’t again.

New musicSun 7:15–9:30pm

West Oakland Sound Series: Jean Carla Rodea Quartet

Dresher Ensemble Studio · West Oakland
$20 · free for students, seniors, underemployed

An electroacoustic quartet improvising off Rodea’s scores — voice and electronics, Kyle Bruckmann on oboe, Kanoko Nishi-Smith on koto, Fred Lonberg-Holm on cello. Second set is Aine Nakamura’s voice-and-body work with clarinet and computer. Fifty seats in a warehouse.

Bernal Heights Hillwide Garage Sale

All over Bernal Heights · SF
Free · official map at hillwide.com

A hundred-plus households on the hill selling at once, always on the second Saturday of August, with a printed and online map so you can plan a route. The single best day of junk-hunting in the city, and it benefits the Bernal Heights Neighborhood Center.

Chabot Hike & Sip

Chabot Space & Science Center · Oakland Hills
$40 · 21+ · includes 2 drinks + charcuterie

Festivals & Markets

6 events

Two big free cultural festivals anchor the weekend, plus a once-a-year studio sale that is worth planning around.

TOP PICK★ CRITICS’ · SF Standard & 7x7
Cultural festivalSat & Sun 11am–5pm

Pistahan Parade & Festival (33rd)

Yerba Buena Gardens · SoMa, SF
Free · parade Sat 11am from Civic Center

The largest Filipino cultural festival on the West Coast, organised into eight themed pavilions — Art, Culinary, Dance, Heritage, Innovation — plus an exhibit hall, artisan marketplace and near-continuous folk dance, jazz and martial arts.

Japantown & Cultural Centers

4 events

Japantown carries this lane — the Korean, Chinese and Slavic centers are all genuinely empty this weekend, verified at source.

🕊️
TOP PICK✦ Director present · free
Film + commemorationSun 1–3pm

A Remembrance for Peace: White Light / Black Rain

Konko Church of San Francisco · Japantown, SF
Free · register by Fri noon

Steven Okazaki introduces his Emmy-winning documentary on Hiroshima and Nagasaki, told through fourteen hibakusha, on the 81st-anniversary weekend. Presented by the Nichi Bei Foundation and Friends of Hibakusha in a church rather than a cinema, which changes the room entirely.

Notes & things to double-check

Times were read off each venue’s own event page on August 6, 2026. A few to confirm before you go: Shotgun Players — the Sunday 5pm curtain for Iphigenia in Splott is inferred (their ticketing calendar isn’t machine-readable); call 510.841.6500 x303. Sunday is also a masked performance with a post-show conversation. Central Works — Saturday’s Prince Part 1 and Sunday’s Part 2 are fully reserved; a waitlist opens 30 minutes before curtain. Lick Observatory — Friday is sold out, Saturday was still available. Chabot and Foothill telescope nights are clear-sky-only; Chabot’s refractors close above 90% humidity, so check their weather page the day of. The Marsh SF (Dan Hoyle, Fri) shows sold out with a waitlist, so it isn’t carded above. PlayGround Free-Play runs a dozen premieres at staggered times — check the festival page for what’s starting when. A handful of cards (Klee, Cyrus Chestnut, the Electronics Flea, Hillwide, Creative Growth, SF Shakes, Golden Sardine, When Light Listens) show the category gradient because those sites publish no usable share image.

Deliberately skipped

Outside Lands and its entire satellite ecosystem of after-parties — a large-scale music festival is squarely off your list, though it shapes where everything else in this guide sits. Also cut: Circus Æternus at the Midway (billed as circus, actually fifteen-plus DJs), the Grateful Dead Meet-Up at the Movies concert simulcast, arena and stadium shows (Ed Sheeran, Jill Scott, Dark Star Orchestra), the R&B bills at Yoshi’s, the Alcatraz-to-Angel-Island swim (a gated endurance event), and routine first-run multiplex programming. Per your standing note this session, LGBTQ/Pride-specific programming was deprioritised — that removed a Castro gallery opening, the SOMArts ballroom function, a Berkeley pre-Pride picnic and the Roxie’s Drunken Noodles run from the spotlight. Two genuinely good finds were dropped for want of a linkable event page: the 16mm Underworld with live accompaniment at Niles (their site is an unreadable app) and the First-Friday “Alley Poems” gathering in Kerouac Alley (Instagram only).
